_what: The rung ladder, and the model each rung binds to. Data, not prose: the resolver in gyroscope/routing.py compares `rank` and never a name, so renaming a rung cannot reorder the ladder and adding one cannot be done by spelling.
_why: Codex is the workhorse. Per dollar it buys far more capacity than the dear tiers, so it holds every rung whose failure heals -- a bad bulk unit is caught by the check that was going to run anyway, and redoing it costs another cheap unit. Intelligence is the only edge worth paying for, and it is worth paying for only where the failure does NOT heal: where the wrong move destroys the evidence it was wrong, or cascades into work that inherits it. That is the whole allocation, and `pays_for` states it per rung.
_limit: NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN PROBED. This file is a claim about which routes exist, and a claim is not a reachable route. `routing.plan()` refuses to return a route it has not seen a live probe for, which is the only place a binding becomes evidence. Treat a `model` string here as the name someone wrote down, not as a destination known to answer.
_resolution_note: First hit wins, and the packaged copy is last: a repository or an account that states its own ladder overrides the shipped one rather than merging with it. A merge would let a repository silently inherit a rung it never declared, and the rung it inherits is the one that decides what gets paid for.

rungs.name: bulk
rungs.capability: mechanical breadth -- many near-identical units, each cheap to check and cheap to redo
rungs._heals_because: a wrong unit is caught by the check that was already going to run, and the repair is one more unit of the same cost
rungs._effort_note: Effort inside a rung is DOSE, not capability: it never reorders the ladder, and it is spent smallest-first. Only this rung carries sub-levels, because it is the only one where the same capability answers a wide range of doses.

rungs.name: moderate
rungs.capability: implementation against a settled design -- the shape is decided, the work is to build it
admits: test authoring against a stated contract
rungs._heals_because: the design that would have been expensive to get wrong was settled before this rung was reached; a wrong implementation shows up as a red check

rungs.name: hard
rungs.capability: hard or novel -- the design is not settled, and the judgment is the work
admits: diagnosing a failure whose cause is not yet named
rungs._heals_because: a wrong judgment here is still visible before anything is built on it -- which is exactly what stops holding one rung up

rungs.name: extreme
rungs.capability: extreme or cross-cutting -- the unit's blast radius crosses subsystem boundaries
admits: anything later work will inherit without re-deriving
rungs._heals_because: by the time it is wrong, other work has already been built on it; the repair is not this unit, it is everything downstream of it

rungs.name: pivotal
rungs.capability: PIVOTAL and reasoning-heavy -- what the rest of the run inherits, where the failure does not heal
admits: bulk verification of a clause that is being trusted
rungs._heals_because: the wrong move destroys the evidence that it was wrong, so there is no later observation that reports it

triggers.name: bulk
triggers.because: many near-identical units, each cheap to redo

triggers.name: implementation
triggers.because: the design is settled; building it is the work

triggers.name: difficult_judgment
triggers.because: the highest band below the top: judgment is the work, but a wrong call is still visible before anything rests on it

triggers.name: novel
triggers.because: no settled shape to build against

triggers.name: cross_cutting
triggers.because: the blast radius leaves the subsystem, so the repair is not this unit

triggers.name: cascading
triggers.because: later work inherits the error and re-states it, so the cost grows after the mistake rather than at it

triggers.name: unhealing
triggers.because: the wrong move destroys the evidence it was wrong; nothing downstream reports it

triggers.name: bulk_verification_of_trusted_clauses
triggers.because: this is the trap the ladder exists to name. It LOOKS like bulk -- many near-identical clauses, each individually cheap -- and it is not, because the output is a decision to TRUST. A clause wrongly waved through is then relied on, and everything that relies on it is built on a check nobody will run again. The failure does not heal, so it takes the top rung and not the bottom one.

_triggers_note: Triggers fall UPWARD only. A unit's rung is the highest of the one it states and the floor of every trigger that is live on it -- so unhealing beats bulk, and no trigger can ever pull a unit down to a cheaper rung than it declared. With no trigger live, the unit's stated rung stands.
